requirement:
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
rationale:
The subject `requirements.references.outline_selectors` has one obligation. Habeas must use the TBV outline selector grammar from `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses. The grammar's own clauses belong to the cited requirement, which has its own tests. Here I only checked that the tests apply the grammar to Habeas's source addresses and outlines.

Tests that cover the obligation:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reading_paths]` checks the source-address path. `OutlineData::new` accepts `""`, `fn[kept]` and `mod[a%2Fb]/fn[kept]`, and it preserves the selector text. It rejects `fn[missing`, `fn[bad%ZZ]` and `/fn[kept]`. This covers the empty root selector, percent-encoded names, and malformed selectors, all without reading the path.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` checks that Habeas's generated selectors have the grammar's form and that they resolve. The forms covered are `kind[name]`, nested paths, `impl[Thing/Trait]`, percent-encoded `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`, and `#1` and `#2` disambiguation. It also checks that the empty selector resolves to the root, that an ambiguous selector fails, and that a missing selector fails.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes]` checks the `kind@<12 hex>` form for `use` nodes. It checks that selectors survive an insertion, that a changed node no longer resolves, and that duplicate anonymous nodes get `#N`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` checks that identical `line@hash` selectors resolve. It also checks that the hash ignores whitespace differences.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits]` checks that an anonymous container's selector uses its identity hash and still resolves after its descendants are edited.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs#fn[paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges]` checks that Markdown anonymous nodes get `kind@` plus 12 characters and that every selector round-trips through `resolve`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent]` checks the error behavior. A missing selector gives "no outline node matches", and a malformed percent escape gives "invalid outline selector".

These tests cover the supported source kinds (Rust, Markdown, YAML and plain text), selector generation and resolution, and address validation. I found no gap.

text: An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
